title: The ack is lost after the work: the broker redelivers, the dedupe table stops the second charge
captions: The broker delivers message m42 to the consumer. The message asks it to charge order 7. It carries a unique message ID.
In one database transaction, the consumer records that it has seen m42 and saves the charge. The transaction commits. The work is done.
The consumer sends its ack, but the ack is lost, or the consumer crashes first. The broker cannot tell this apart from a message that was never handled.
So the broker does the only safe thing. It delivers m42 again, with the same message ID.
The insert of m42 hits the unique key and adds 0 rows. The consumer skips the work and acks. The order is charged once.
